import pandas as pd

# File paths for the source CSV files
source0_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_0.csv"
source1_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_1.csv"
source2_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_2.csv"

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the first numerical index column
df0 = pd.read_csv(source0_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']
df1 = pd.read_csv(source1_path, index_col=0)  # ['movie_id', 'title', 'genres']
df2 = pd.read_csv(source2_path, index_col=0)  # ['user_id', 'gender', 'age', 'occupation', 'zip']

# Step 1: Join df0 and df1 on 'movie_id' to get title for each rating record
df0_1 = pd.merge(df0, df1[['movie_id', 'title']], on='movie_id', how='left')

# Step 2: Join the above result with df2 on 'user_id' to get user demographic info
df_all = pd.merge(df0_1, df2[['user_id', 'age', 'occupation']], on='user_id', how='left')

# Step 3: Prepare the final DataFrame with the target schema:
# ['title': string, 'user_id': float, 'age': float, 'occupation': float, 'movie_id': integer, 'rating': float, 'timestamp': float]

# Convert columns to required types:
# - title: string (already string)
# - user_id: float (source is int, convert to float)
# - age: float (source is int, convert to float)
# - occupation: float (source is int, convert to float)
# - movie_id: integer (should be int)
# - rating: float (source is int, convert to float)
# - timestamp: float (source is int, convert to float)

df_all['title'] = df_all['title'].astype(str)
df_all['user_id'] = df_all['user_id'].astype(float)
df_all['age'] = df_all['age'].astype(float)
df_all['occupation'] = df_all['occupation'].astype(float)
df_all['movie_id'] = df_all['movie_id'].astype(int)
df_all['rating'] = df_all['rating'].astype(float)
df_all['timestamp'] = df_all['timestamp'].astype(float)

# Select and reorder columns to match target schema exactly
df_target = df_all[['title', 'user_id', 'age', 'occupation', 'movie_id', 'rating', 'timestamp']]

# Write the result to the specified output path
output_path = "autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource_cot.csv"
df_target.to_csv(output_path, index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source3_2_0 and Source3_2_1 on movie_id
result = pd.merge(source0, source1, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join the above result with Source3_2_2 on user_id
result = pd.merge(result, source2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Group by title and movie_id (leftmost non-float unique columns in target)
# Aggregate other columns by mean as target shows float averages for user_id, age, occupation, rating, timestamp
grouped = result.groupby(["title", "movie_id"], as_index=False).agg({
    "user_id": "mean",
    "age": "mean",
    "occupation": "mean",
    "rating": "mean",
    "timestamp": "mean"
})

# Reorder columns to match target schema exactly
final = grouped[["title", "user_id", "age", "occupation", "movie_id", "rating", "timestamp"]]

# Write to target file
final.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_2/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
